limitations: Static review of the frozen snapshot only. I ran no tests and make no claim that any test passes.

I did not see the bodies of reconstruct_interval, verify_bootstrap, or the transport helpers. I take the reported exception sources (RuntimeError from the API and observation layer, sqlite3.Error from the temporary database) from the earlier review and the task statement.

I could not confirm that the new `patch('sqlite3.connect', ...)` test hits the reconstruction boundary. It does only if the archive module calls `sqlite3.connect` through the module attribute and nothing earlier in the path uses it. If either assumption is wrong, the test would fail loudly instead of passing silently, so it cannot hide a defect.
I accepted the disproof of the original interval-ordering finding as given. The archive.py lines 1110 and discovery.py lines 721-722 you supplied both enforce `coverage_from <= interval_end`.
review_summary: The accepted structured-error finding is fixed. Both handlers, `reporting_readiness` (line 64) and `reporting_main` (line 82), now also catch `RuntimeError` and `sqlite3.Error`. `import sqlite3` sits before the `try` in each function, so the new name is always bound when the handler runs. On a caught failure, the result carries only the fixed reason strings. No exception text reaches the JSON output, and `reporting_main` still returns 1 when any check failed. The new tests cover both paths. The first raises a `RuntimeError` carrying a private diagnostic from the state API and asserts that `protected_origin` is `failed` and the text is absent. The second injects a `sqlite3.OperationalError` at `sqlite3.connect` and asserts the same for `retained_interval`. The diff does not change the other checks or the `--policy` path. I see no new actionable defect. The original ordering finding is withdrawn, since the validators you pointed to enforce the check.
